chapter: Boyhood and the West End camps
title: Trumpet duels on the wharfs at the West End camps
summary: Trumpet men blew at each other from the camp wharfs at West End, and a dollar bought a whole Saturday night.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Did you ever hear any good contests like that? Oh, I did.

Man, I heard some contests out of this world, especially when they had all those camps at West End. The Lillian Cottage, the Dixie Cottage, American Club. And man, they'd come out on the wharf, the trumpet men would come out on the wharf. The camps had big long wharfs leading to them, you know. They'd come out there and blow at one another. I even got tied up in some of them duels myself. We used to play a lot at the Lillian Cottage out at West End. And those bands would come in the American Club or the Norma Villa, right near there. You couldn't help with getting a duel because once you'd start playing, they'd try to come out on the wharf and play at you. That was something, man. For a dollar, you could go out there on a Saturday evening with your girl if you wanted, eat and drink all Saturday night and dancing from 9 to 6 Sunday for a dollar.
A dollar and a couple. Nine to six, that's six o'clock at night?
